title: When the Harvest Wakes
premise: Ansel Vane takes a teaching post in the isolated farming town of Hollowmere, where students vanish one by one and no one will say why. The town's founding families keep an old bargain with something beneath the fields, paid each harvest, and Ansel's arrival completes a count begun generations ago. When their childhood imaginary friend appears on their porch—aged not a day, and hungry for company—Ansel learns they were promised to the harvest as a child. To break the bargain, Ansel must expose the truth to the families who benefit from it, knowing some would rather feed the fields than lose their standing. In the end, Ansel burns the school's ledger of names, severing the count, but the friend stays behind on the porch, waiting for someone else to come home.
about_author: Marguerite Halloran is a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in farming communities where old agreements were never written down. She writes horror about the quiet violence of belonging.

chapters.title: The Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Ansel Vane arrives in Hollowmere and takes the teaching post at a school where three seats sit empty and no one asks after the missing children. POV: Ansel. They notice doors being counted aloud by neighbors each dusk, and chalk tallies appearing on the schoolhouse wall overnight. The emotional beat is unease dressed as welcome—the town is kind, but its kindness has rules.

chapters.title: What Waited on the Porch
chapters.summary: Ansel's childhood imaginary friend, Wick, appears on their porch exactly as remembered, and knows things about Hollowmere no stranger should. POV: Ansel, with flashbacks to the promise made by their grandmother. Wick reveals Ansel was pledged to the harvest before they could walk. The emotional beat is dread braided with longing—Wick is terrifying and the only warmth Ansel has ever trusted.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Ansel finds the school's hidden ledger: every vanished child recorded in a founding family's hand, including their own name dated decades ago. POV: alternating Ansel and matriarch Odette Crane, who believes the bargain keeps her family fed and powerful. Ansel tries to warn parents; loyalty to tradition beats truth. The emotional beat is betrayal—the corruption of power shown through mothers who choose the field over their own children.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: On harvest night, Ansel races to get the remaining families out while Wick holds the field's attention, love against duty made flesh. POV: Ansel. They burn the ledger mid-count, breaking the tally, and the ground goes still—but Wick cannot leave with them. The emotional beat is grief and resolve: Ansel saves the town's children, loses their oldest friend, and drives away past a porch where something new is waiting.
